verdict: Cargo Code is mathematically sound but experientially a dashboard. Seven simultaneous panels, a punitive timer that punishes the slow careful reasoning we are trying to teach, a tally strip that quietly gives away the answer, and a world that never visibly runs on multiplication — the claw fires because a form was filled correctly, not because the math did anything. The bluff mechanic is the one genuinely clever idea, but it cannot rescue a core loop that feels like data entry under a stopwatch. A nine-year-old sees buttons, not a world. Pivot.
strongestExistingQuality: The 'Call the Bluff' verdict mechanic — using a self-built array as evidence to disprove a rival's false product is real mathematical argumentation, and it should be reincarnated in the new direction as a late-game skill.
largestCreativeFailure: Multiplication has no visible power in the world. The array is decorative, the product is typed into a box, and the reward (a claw animation) is disconnected from the quantity itself. Add the race-timer that punishes deliberation, and the game actively fights its own learning goal.

creativeDirection.title: Lanternlift: Raise the Sky Town
creativeDirection.openingPromise: A floating town has fallen into the fog, split into stranded districts. You are the new Lantern Rigger. Every paper lantern gives exactly one lift. String lanterns onto balloon nets in equal rows, call the total lift out loud as an equation, and pull the lever — if your math is true, a whole district rises out of the fog and docks back into the sky.
creativeDirection.coreLoop: 1) Read a lift order (a short situation: how many nets, how many lanterns each — the wording varies and sometimes swaps order). 2) Rig the load: tap a net to add it as a row, tap a net to fill it with lanterns — the living array glows brighter with every lantern. 3) Declare your lift: complete the equation nets × lanterns = total on the big brass gauge. 4) Pull the release lever. The balloon rises row by row — each row adds exactly its lanterns' worth of height, skip-counting visibly up the measuring mast — and either docks perfectly at the target height or visibly overshoots/undershoots, inviting adjustment.
creativeDirection.mathAsPower: The product IS the lift. 4 nets of 6 lanterns produces exactly 24 meters of rise, animated as four pulses of +6 climbing the mast — the child literally watches repeated addition become multiplication. A wrong product means the district physically stops short in the fog or floats past the dock. The array is not an illustration of the answer; it is the engine.
creativeDirection.stakes: Warm, not punitive: stranded townsfolk wave from foggy rooftops, and every successful lift snaps a district back into the glowing sky-town silhouette at the top of the screen. The town map fills in delivery by delivery — the child can always see how close the town is to being whole. No countdown, no rival stealing progress.
creativeDirection.consequenceAndRecovery: A mismatched lift is never a fail-state — it is information. The balloon rises to exactly what the child built, the mast shows both the reached height and the target height, and a gentle voice line says 'Short by 6 — check your rows.' The child adds or removes lanterns and pulls again, unlimited tries. After two misses on the same order, one net unspools its lanterns one at a time as a counting scaffold, then re-bundles. First-try perfect lifts earn a gold pennant; retried lifts still succeed and still raise the district.
progression: Act 1 — The Low Docks (products to 25): explicit orders ('3 nets, 5 lanterns each'), child builds the full array and writes the whole equation; mast shows skip-count pulses every time.

Act 2 — The Wind Terraces (factors to 9): orders arrive in varied and reversed language with distractor numbers ('The rigger, age 41, needs 6 lanterns in every net across 7 nets'); some loads arrive pre-rigged and the child must read the array and write the equation instead of building it; the gauge stops pre-filling factors.

Act 3 — The High Spire (missing factors and judgment): 'We need 24 lift and nets hold 6 — how many nets?'; the returning Bluff mechanic as 'Foreman Moro's Manifests' — a lazy foreman posts claimed totals ('5 nets × 7 each = 32, sign here') and the child rigs the true array as evidence to approve or reject the manifest.
Finale — The Festival Load: the child designs their own load to hit a target lift with multiple valid arrays (e.g., reach exactly 36), proving multiplicative fluency by choosing factors freely.
creativeDirection.worldReaction: Every lantern added plays a rising kalimba note pitched to its count, so a row of 6 is heard as an ascending six-note run — an audible group. Docked districts light their windows, add tiny cheering silhouettes, and permanently change the skyline. Rejecting a false manifest makes Foreman Moro tear it up while the crowd laughs. The sky itself brightens from deep fog-blue toward festival dusk as the town reassembles.
creativeDirection.payoff: When the final district docks, the whole reunited sky-town erupts into the Lantern Festival: every equation the child solved reappears as a constellation of lanterns released into the night sky, each one labeled with its equation (4 × 6 = 24), spelling out the child's complete case history as fireworks of their own reasoning. A rigger's license certificate shows gold pennants earned and hardest lift completed.
creativeDirection.replay: Orders are procedurally generated per run. A post-finale 'Master Rigger' mode remixes: more missing-factor orders, more false manifests, and open 'design your own load' targets. Gold-pennant hunting (first-try perfect lifts on every district) gives fluent kids a reason to run it again fast and clean.
creativeDirection.visualAndSoundDirection: Studio-Ghibli night harbor in the clouds: deep indigo fog below, warm amber paper lanterns, brass gauge and rope textures, hand-painted district silhouettes. One focal scene at a time — order card, rig, gauge, lever, mast — never seven panels. Sound: soft wind bed, kalimba notes per lantern (pitch encodes count), a low rope-creak on lever pull, a swelling chord plus crowd murmur on perfect dock, and a kind descending 'hmm' (never a buzzer) on a miss.

opusBuilderBrief: Build 'Lanternlift: Raise the Sky Town' as a single self-contained HTML file for a 1365×768 iframe, touch- and mouse-friendly with all tap targets ≥56px. STRUCTURE: intro overlay (title, 3-sentence promise, big START), three acts of 4 orders each plus a Festival finale (13 lifts total), end overlay with constellation payoff and replay button. LAYOUT: one focal composition — top: sky-town silhouette that fills in per docked district (town map = progress bar); center-left: order card with the situation text (groups and per-group amounts subtly highlighted in Act 1 only); center: the balloon rig where tapping '+ Net' adds a horizontal net row and tapping a net adds/removes lanterns in it (this IS the array — rows are nets/groups, lanterns per row are the group size, max 9×9); center-right: measuring mast with target height marker; bottom: brass gauge showing __ × __ = __ with a large keypad, and one big LEVER button. CORE MECHANIC: on lever pull, validate that the built array matches the order AND the equation matches the array AND product is correct; animate the balloon rising with one pulse per row, each pulse adding that row's lantern count to a running total on the mast (skip-counting made visible, ~400ms per pulse); perfect match docks the district with chord + window lights; mismatch rises to the actual built total, shows 'Short by N' or 'Over by N', and returns for free retry. SCAFFOLD: after 2 misses on an order, animate one net unspooling its lanterns counted one-by-one. PROGRESSION: Act 1 explicit orders products≤25, full build; Act 2 factors≤9, varied/reversed wording with distractor numbers, alternate pre-built arrays the child must read and write the equation for; Act 3 missing-factor orders (given total and one factor) and 2 'Foreman Moro manifest' judgments where a claimed product (55% false, off by 1–20%) must be APPROVED or REJECTED using a self-built array as evidence — rejecting a lie or approving a truth succeeds; Finale: hit an exact target lift with any valid factor pair. NO countdown timers, NO answer-revealing tally strip. Gold pennant per first-try perfect lift, tracked on end screen. SOUND via WebAudio: per-lantern kalimba notes rising in pitch with count within a row, rope creak on lever, warm chord on dock, gentle descending tone on miss. Payoff: released lantern constellation showing every solved equation floating upward. Keep all interactive logic mathematically airtight: the product must always equal rows × per-row as built, and the mast animation must always sum row pulses to exactly the product.
